key_insight: Textual feedback provides a middle ground between sparse binary rewards and costly demonstrations: it is richer than a single-bit signal yet cheaper and more scalable than full demonstrations, enabling denser, human-native supervision for policy learning.
problem_solved: RL training for language and decision agents relies on either very sparse rewards or expensive demonstrations; this paper addresses how to obtain richer, scalable supervision that improves learning without requiring full expert demonstrations.
method: Collect natural-language feedback associated with rollouts or model outputs (human or crowd-sourced).
Train models to interpret text feedback into dense training signals (e.g., learned reward or loss shaping).
Use the derived dense signals to update policies (via RL fine-tuning or supervised objectives), closing the gap between scalar rewards and demonstrations.
impact: Provides a practical, scalable way to improve sample efficiency and alignment in RL systems by leveraging abundant human-language feedback—reducing annotation cost while yielding richer supervision that is easy to inspect and improve.
visual_elements: Spectrum diagram comparing binary rewards ← text feedback ← demonstrations (showing richness vs cost).
Pipeline flowchart: agent rollout → human text feedback → feedback-to-reward model → policy update.
Before/after schematic learning curve (conceptual) showing faster/better learning with text feedback vs binary reward.
Icon set: speech bubble (text feedback), single-bit thumbs (binary reward), full demo icon (expensive), and a gear/robot for the agent.
paper_title: Expanding the Capabilities of Reinforcement Learning via Text Feedback
paper_authors: Yuda Song, Lili Chen, Fahim Tajwar, Remi Munos, Deepak Pathak
